interest: Shows postwar rice diplomacy for Japan via FAO, IEFC, Burma and Siam, including a proposed Japan-rice-for-China barter scheme.
overview: This file (894.61317, covering April 1947 through December 1949) documents the severe food supply challenges facing occupied Japan, international efforts to secure emergency rice imports, and the eventual domestic agricultural recovery under the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP). In 1947 and 1948, acute food deficits threatened Japan's economic and political stability, forcing U.S. and occupation authorities to navigate worldwide grain shortages, complex international allocations through the International Emergency Food Council (IEFC), regional unrest in Burma, and innovative triangular barter schemes involving Siamese rice, Japanese manufactured goods, and ECA dollars. By late 1949, the focus shifted to documenting a dramatic resurgence in domestic staple food production, driven by massive fertilizer imports, scientific pest and disease control, improved seed stock, and agrarian cooperation that brought rice yields to their highest levels since 1942.

subfiles.about: Requests background memoranda on Japanese and Korean rice production, distribution, and agrarian policies for an upcoming FAO rice study meeting in Delhi.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of State Dean Acheson (Department of State)
subfiles.summary: State instructs SCAP and USAFIK to prepare ten background memos on Japanese and Korean rice for an FAO Delhi conference, covering production, forecasting, storage, prices, tenure, and nutrition, urging declassification of relevant reports.
subfiles.title: State Department Telegram to SCAP on FAO Rice Conference Preparations
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP), Tokyo

subfiles.about: Transmits extracts from Bangkok concerning the establishment of a Siamese government allocation bureau and shipping committee for rice exports.
subfiles.from: Secretary of State George C. Marshall (Department of State)
subfiles.summary: State forwards Bangkok's report on a new Siamese Allocation Bureau replacing the Rice Commission, distributing export rice per IEFC quotas directly to shippers, instructing Manila to notify the Philippines.
subfiles.title: State Department Telegram to Manila Embassy on Siamese Rice Allocation Machinery

subfiles.about: Urges approval of a 100,000-ton Siamese rice import allocation to alleviate Japan's severe summer staple food ration deficit.
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP), Tokyo
subfiles.summary: SCAP urges 100,000 tons of Siamese rice for Japan, noting Japan can accept broken or glutinous grades and that summer arrival would ease a severe ration shortfall, with shipping already arranged via Bangkok.
subfiles.title: SCAP Telegram on Urgent Need for Siamese Rice Imports
subfiles.to: Department of the Army and Department of State

subfiles.about: Reports that Burmese rice exports are severely curtailed by insurgent unrest and cannot be spared for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Rangoon's attaché tells SCAP Burmese rice exports to Japan are hopeless, as insurgency has cut output below existing IEFC commitments to India, Ceylon, Malaya, and China.
subfiles.title: Rangoon Military Attaché Telegram on Impossibility of Burmese Rice Shipments to Japan
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP), Tokyo

subfiles.about: Records inter-agency discussions on allocating rice to Japan through the IEFC and an Army proposal for triangular trade involving Siam, Japan, and China.
subfiles.from: W. S. McCornick (Division of Commercial Policy, Department of State)
subfiles.summary: State, Army, and ECA discuss a triangular trade: Japan's Board of Trade would barter manufactured goods for Siamese rice, reselling it to ECA for dollars toward China aid, though China objections and surplus-rice rules pose risks.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum of Conversation on IEFC Rice Allocation and Triangular Trade

subfiles.about: Transmits a GHQ Far East Command press release estimating the 1949 Japanese rice harvest at 9,832,000 metric tons.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald (U.S. Political Adviser to SCAP, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: USPOLAD Tokyo forwards SCAP's 1949 rice crop estimate of 9,832,000 metric tons, 5% above the prewar average despite typhoon and pest damage in Kyushu, Tohoku, and Kinki, the highest since 1942.
subfiles.title: USPOLAD Tokyo Airgram Transmitting 1949 Japanese Rice Crop Estimate

subfiles.about: Transmits a GHQ SCAP press release documenting postwar recovery in Japan's staple food production up to 1949.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald (U.S. Political Adviser to SCAP, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: USPOLAD Tokyo forwards SCAP's report on Japan's staple food recovery from 9.9 million tons in 1945 to 14.4 million in 1949, crediting fertilizer, better seed, and pest control, urging continued cooperation and sound incentives.
subfiles.title: USPOLAD Tokyo Airgram on Postwar Japanese Staple Food Production Recovery
